thread:
maria: FYI staging data-uploader pods started CrashLoopBackOff after the infra TF apply. Init container fails trying to read a token file. Logs: `open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory` — we rolled a helm change to the ksa earlier today, any quick ideas?

priya: Did TF flip `automountServiceAccountToken` on the pod spec? If the pod has automount disabled the token won't be auto-mounted.

maria: Helm values we applied (trimmed):

```
serviceAccount:
  name: data-uploader-ksa
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-data-upload

pod:
  automountServiceAccountToken: false
initContainers:
  - name: fetch-creds
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/fetch-token.sh /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"]
```

tom: That explains it. You turned off automount but the init container is still reading the legacy token path. Two options: enable automount on the pod/deployment, or switch to an explicit projected `serviceAccountToken` volume and mount it where the init container expects it.

alex: Quick example of mounting a projected token to be explicit (and secure):

```
volumes:
- name: sa-token
  projected:
    sources:
    - serviceAccountToken:
        path: token
        expirationSeconds: 3600

containers:
- name: init
  volumeMounts:
  - name: sa-token
    mountPath: /etc/svc-token
    readOnly: true
```

Then update the init command to read `/etc/svc-token/token`. Keeps automount disabled and avoids surprise token mounts.

priya: Also check that the IRSA annotation is on the ServiceAccount object the pod is using. If TF or chart templating accidentally put the annotation at the namespace level or on a different SA the pod won't assume the role. `kubectl get sa data-uploader-ksa -n staging -o yaml` will show it.

maria: Running checks now. `kubectl describe pod data-uploader-5f9c8 -n staging` shows no projected volumes and the SA is present but no token path mounted. SA YAML shows the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation is present.

tom: Fast mitigation (staging): you can flip automount back on at the deployment level so pods inherit it without changing helm values: `kubectl patch deploy data-uploader -n staging -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"automountServiceAccountToken":true}}}}'` — do that if you need immediate recovery.

maria: Patching now.

deploy-bot: kubectl patch deployment/data-uploader -n staging replaced

maria: Pod restarted and init container succeeded, app Ready. Thanks.

alex: For the long-term fix open a small PR to: 1) update the init image entrypoint to accept a configurable token path (env var like PROJECTED_TOKEN_PATH), 2) add optional volume templates in our helm chart so consumers can opt into projecting the SA token. Also add a note in the chart README about automount implications.

priya: SGTM. Also add a test to our helm lint/ci that renders values with `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and checks that any initContainers that need tokens have corresponding volumes/mounts. Catches this class of bug earlier.

maria: Will open PR and link to #pr-review. Leaving staging with automount=true for now until the chart change lands. I'll include the `kubectl` outputs in the PR for context.

tom: Nice narrow scope. Also consider using a projected `expirationSeconds` short TTL in staging while you iterate (e.g., 600s) so tokens rotate.

maria: Good call. Will do. Closing the loop here, thanks all :thumbsup:
